units.literal: They fought Meng Fangli at Tongdi with an unfavorable outcome, and the Martial Emperor then ordered Ke Xiu to lead troops forward in succession.

units.zh: 方立求援於鎮州，王鎔出師三萬援之，克修軍退。
units.en: Fangli appealed to Zhenzhou for help. Wang Rong marched out thirty thousand men to relieve him, and Ke Xiu's army fell back.
units.literal: Fangli sought aid from Zhenzhou; Wang Rong marched out thirty thousand men to relieve him, and Ke Xiu's army withdrew.

units.zh: 及李罕之來歸，武皇授以澤州刺史，與克修合勢進攻河陽，連歲出師，以苦懷、孟。
units.en: When Li Hanzhi defected to Li Keyong, he was made prefect of Zezhou and joined Ke Xiu in a combined offensive against Heyang. Campaigning year after year, they wore down the Huai and Meng factions.
units.literal: When Li Hanzhi came over to our side, the Martial Emperor appointed him prefect of Zezhou. Together with Ke Xiu he combined forces to attack Heyang, campaigning year after year to wear down Huai and Meng.

units.zh: 大順初，潞帥李克修卒，克恭代為昭義節度使。
units.en: Early in the Dashun era, after the Lu commander Ke Xiu died, Ke Gong succeeded him as military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
units.literal: At the beginning of Dazhun, the Lu commander Ke Xiu died, and Ke Gong replaced him as military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

units.zh: 潞人素便克修之簡正，惡克恭之恣縱，又以克修非罪暴卒，人士離心。
units.en: The people of Lu had long valued Ke Xiu's plain, upright rule and resented Ke Gong's excesses. Ke Xiu's sudden death, though he was innocent of wrongdoing, also alienated the gentry and commoners.
units.literal: The people of Lu had long been accustomed to Ke Xiu's simplicity and rectitude and hated Ke Gong's wanton indulgence. Moreover, because Ke Xiu had died violently though guiltless, officials and commoners lost heart.

units.zh: 故昭義節度使李嗣昭、故幽州節度使周德威、故汴州節度使符存審，並配饗莊宗廟廷。
units.en: Li Sizhao, Zhou Dewei, and Fu Cunshen were given collateral offerings in Zhuangzong's temple.
units.literal: The late Zhaoyi military commissioner Li Sizhao, late Youzhou military commissioner Zhou Dewei, late Bianzhou military commissioner Fu Cunshen—all were collaterally offered in Zhuangzong's temple hall.

units.zh: 戊午，荊南奏：「東川董璋領兵至漢州，西川孟知祥出兵逆戰，璋大敗，得部下人二十餘，走入東川城，尋為前陵州刺史王暉所殺，孟知祥已入梓州。」
units.en: On wuwu Jingnan reported: "Dong Zhang of eastern Sichuan had marched on Han; Meng Zhixiang of western Sichuan met him; Zhang was routed with only twenty-odd followers, fled into the eastern Sichuan capital, was killed by former Ling prefect Wang Hui, and Meng Zhixiang had entered Zizhou."
units.literal: On wuwu, Jingnan memorialized: "Eastern Sichuan's Dong Zhang led troops to Hanzhou; western Sichuan's Meng Zhixiang sent troops to meet him in battle; Zhang was utterly defeated, taking only twenty-odd of his men; he fled into the eastern Sichuan city and was soon killed by former Ling prefect Wang Hui; Meng Zhixiang has already entered Zizhou."

units.zh: 可舉慮其窺伺山東，終為己患，遂遣使構雲中赫連鐸乘其背，則與鎮州合謀舉兵，兼言易、定是燕、趙之餘，雲得其地則正其疆理而分之。
units.en: Keju feared that Keyong would turn his ambitions toward the eastern provinces and become a lasting threat. He sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to attack Keyong from the rear, then conspired with the forces of Zhenzhou to raise troops. He argued that Yizhou and Dingzhou were the last holdings of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yunzhong gained those lands their boundaries could be redrawn and the territory divided.
units.literal: Keju feared that Keyong would watch for an opening in the Shandong region and in the end become a threat to him; he therefore sent envoys to incite Helian Duo of Yunzhong to strike from the rear, then conspired with Zhenzhou to raise troops, also saying that Yi and Ding were the remnant territories of Yan and Zhao, and that if Yun gained those lands their boundaries could be rectified and divided.

units.zh: 赫連鐸據雲中，屢引匡威與河東爭雲、代，並兵積年。
units.en: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into conflict with Hedong over Yunzhou and Daizhou; their armies fought for years.
units.literal: Helian Duo held Yunzhong and repeatedly drew Kuangwei into contest with Hedong over Yun and Dai; their armies clashed for years.

units.zh: 初，孟方立之亂，居受以澤、潞歸於武皇，至是孟遷以邢、洺納降，復任為牙將，居受懼其圖己，乃叛，殺克恭以結汴人。
units.en: During Meng Fangli's rebellion Jushou had surrendered Ze and Lu to Li Keyong. Now Meng Qian surrendered Xing and Ming and was reappointed a garrison officer. Fearing that Meng Qian would move against him, Jushou rebelled, killed Ke Gong, and sought an alliance with the Liang.
units.literal: Earlier, during Meng Fangli's rebellion, Jushou had surrendered Ze and Lu to the Martial Emperor. Now Meng Qian surrendered Xing and Ming and was reappointed a garrison officer. Jushou feared he would plot against him, therefore rebelled and killed Ke Gong to ally with the Bian.
